name: Worcester
lede: New England's second-largest city, built on hills, mills and three-deckers, and still remaking itself one block at a time.
overview: Worcester is the center of gravity for everything on this sheet. Its neighborhoods range from the Victorian streets around Elm Park to the brick lofts of the Canal District, and almost every one of them has its own main street, its own diner and its own opinion about the others.

For buyers, the city offers the widest spread of housing in the region: condos and lofts near downtown, single-family homes on the West Side and in Tatnuck, and the three-deckers that line whole streets in the older neighborhoods. Many people buy their first home here, and many buy a three-decker to live in one floor and rent the other two.

housing.note: Stacked flats with front and back porches, built for the city's industrial workforce from the late 1800s.
Larger single-family homes concentrated on the West Side and around the parks.

name: Shrewsbury
lede: A town on the east shore of Lake Quinsigamond, with a historic center and neighborhoods that climb away from the water.
overview: Shrewsbury sits directly east of Worcester across Lake Quinsigamond. Route 9 and Route 20 carry most of its traffic and commerce, while the town center keeps the older New England plan of church, library and common.

Housing runs from lakeside cottages and mid-century ranches near the water to larger colonials in newer subdivisions on the town's hills. Buyers often come here wanting a suburban street with a short drive into Worcester.

name: Grafton
lede: A town of villages: a classic common on the hill, mill villages along the water, and a commuter-rail station in the north.
overview: Grafton is organized around several villages rather than one center. Grafton Center, on its hill, has one of the region's best-preserved town commons, ringed by churches and 18th- and 19th-century houses. Mill villages grew along the rivers, and North Grafton has the town's MBTA station.

The housing mix follows that history: antique homes near the common, mill-era houses in the villages, and newer neighborhoods on former farmland. It's a common answer for buyers who want space, character and a train.

housing.note: Federal, Greek Revival and Victorian houses around the common and in the villages.
Smaller worker houses and duplexes along the rivers.

name: Holden
lede: Higher ground northwest of the city: woods, reservoirs, stone walls and a compact town center.
overview: Holden rises toward the hills northwest of Worcester. It's one of the larger towns on this sheet by area, with a lot of it still wooded, and it borders the Wachusett watershed lands.

Most homes are single-family, from older capes near Holden Center to colonials on wooded lots along winding roads. People come here for room, trees and a quieter street, with Worcester a short drive down the hill.

name: Auburn
lede: Where the highways meet, and where a professor launched the first liquid-fueled rocket from a cabbage field in 1926.
overview: Auburn borders Worcester to the south and sits where I-290, I-395, Route 12 and Route 20 come together near the Mass Pike, which makes it one of the most convenient towns on the sheet for driving in any direction.

Its neighborhoods are mostly single-family: capes, ranches and split-levels from the post-war decades, with some newer homes on the town's edges. Robert Goddard's 1926 rocket launch site, on Pakachoag Hill, is marked at the golf course there.

housing.note: Post-war single-family homes on established streets.

name: Millbury
lede: A Blackstone River town with mill history, a hilltop mansion and one of the region's key highway interchanges.
overview: Millbury lies just south of Worcester along the Blackstone River, the river that powered the valley's early industry. Its older villages grew around mills, and the Asa Waters Mansion still overlooks the center.

Route 146 and the Mass Pike meet here, so Millbury attracts buyers who need to reach Worcester, Providence and Boston. Housing includes mill-era homes, mid-century neighborhoods and newer subdivisions.
